newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy outlines plans to cut phone bills.
newsitem.headline: Italy outlines plans to cut phone bills.

text.p: Italian Post and Communications Minister Antonio Maccanico on Wednesday outlined a package of measures designed to cut telephone bills, the ministry said.

A statement said Maccanico and undersecretary Michele Lauria met managers of state telecoms holding Stet to discuss the plans, which it said should reduce annual spending on phone calls by 600 billion lire ($357 million).
The ministry said that taken together with measures passed last October, savings would add up to 1.3 trillion lire.

The planned measures, due to take effect in March, include cheaper local and long-distance calls, a two-phased cut in international tariffs, special offers for Internet users and the introduction of cheap evening rates.
Business rates would go up, as would line rental.
Stet is due to be merged with its main operating unit Telecom Italia ahead of privatisation later this year.
